```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 3.5)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Idea

A deteriorating sensor typically shows (as in your plot after June 2):

1. **More point-to-point noise** (jagged trace, big jumps between consecutive readings)
2. **A drop / drift in level** (readings sag toward the low end)

For each subject and each continuous sensor *session* (split at gaps longer than `session_gap_h`):

1. Compute **rolling-window features**: noise (75th percentile of |Δglucose| between consecutive readings) and level (median glucose).
2. Compare each window to the **session's own baseline** using robust z-scores (median / MAD), so no fixed glucose thresholds are needed.
3. Flag windows with high noise, or with a level drop combined with at least somewhat elevated noise.
4. Merge nearby flagged windows into **segments** and drop segments shorter than `min_seg_h`.

## Settings

```{r config}
cfg <- list(
  window_h        = 12,    # rolling window length (hours)
  step_h          = 3,     # window step (hours)
  max_dt_min      = 20,    # only use consecutive readings <= this far apart for |diff|
  min_cov         = 0.5,   # min fraction of expected readings in a window
  session_gap_h   = 12,    # gap that starts a new sensor session
  min_windows     = 10,    # sessions with fewer windows are skipped (baseline unreliable)
  baseline_days   = NULL,  # NULL = whole session median; or e.g. 5 = use first 5 days as baseline
  z_noise         = 3,     # noise z-score threshold
  z_level         = 3,     # level-drop z-score threshold
  z_level_noise_min = 1,   # noise z needed in addition to a level drop
  merge_gap_h     = 12,    # merge flagged windows separated by less than this
  min_seg_h       = 24     # minimum segment duration to report
)
```

## Input data

Replace this chunk with your own data frame. It needs the columns `subject`, `gluc_time` (POSIXct) and `gl`.

```{r data}
# dat_raw <- readRDS("your_data.rds")   # <- your data here

# ---- demo data (delete when using real data) ----
simulate_cgm <- function(subject, days = 22, det_day = NULL) {
  t <- seq(as.POSIXct("2025-05-14 00:00:00", tz = "UTC"), by = "5 min", length.out = days * 288)
  h <- as.numeric(format(t, "%H")) + as.numeric(format(t, "%M")) / 60
  gl <- 110 + 15 * sin(2 * pi * (h - 8) / 24) +
    as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.95), n = length(t), sd = 4)) + rnorm(length(t), 0, 1.5)
  if (!is.null(det_day)) {
    k <- t >= t[1] + det_day * 86400
    gl[k] <- gl[k] - 15 + rnorm(sum(k), 0, 9)
  }
  tibble(subject = subject, gluc_time = t, gl = gl)
}
set.seed(1)
dat_raw <- bind_rows(simulate_cgm("S1", det_day = 19),
                     simulate_cgm("S2"),
                     simulate_cgm("S3", det_day = 15))
```

```{r prep}
dat <- dat_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(gl), !is.na(gluc_time)) %>%
  arrange(subject, gluc_time) %>%
  distinct(subject, gluc_time, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  group_by(subject) %>%
  mutate(dt_min  = as.numeric(difftime(gluc_time, lag(gluc_time), units = "mins")),
         session = cumsum(is.na(dt_min) | dt_min > cfg$session_gap_h * 60)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Functions

```{r functions}
# Rolling-window features + robust z-scores for ONE subject-session
score_session <- function(d, cfg) {
  t  <- as.numeric(d$gluc_time)
  g  <- d$gl
  tz <- attr(d$gluc_time, "tzone"); if (is.null(tz)) tz <- ""
  dt <- c(NA, diff(t)) / 60
  ad <- ifelse(!is.na(dt) & dt <= cfg$max_dt_min, abs(c(NA, diff(g))), NA)

  W <- cfg$window_h * 3600
  # skip sessions too short to hold min_windows windows (also avoids seq() "wrong sign" error)
  if (max(t) - min(t) < W + (cfg$min_windows - 1) * cfg$step_h * 3600) return(tibble())
  starts <- seq(min(t), max(t) - W, by = cfg$step_h * 3600)
  if (length(starts) < cfg$min_windows) return(tibble())

  step_dt  <- median(dt, na.rm = TRUE)
  expected <- W / 60 / step_dt

  f <- map_dfr(starts, function(s) {
    lo <- findInterval(s,     t, left.open = TRUE) + 1
    hi <- findInterval(s + W, t, left.open = TRUE)
    i  <- if (hi >= lo) lo:hi else integer(0)
    a  <- ad[i]; a <- a[!is.na(a)]
    tibble(win_start = .POSIXct(s, tz = tz),
           win_end   = .POSIXct(s + W, tz = tz),
           cov   = length(i) / expected,
           noise = if (length(a) >= 10) unname(quantile(a, 0.75)) else NA_real_,
           level = if (length(i) > 0) median(g[i]) else NA_real_)
  })

  ok <- f$cov >= cfg$min_cov & !is.na(f$noise) & !is.na(f$level)
  base <- ok
  if (!is.null(cfg$baseline_days)) {
    base <- base & as.numeric(f$win_start) < min(t) + cfg$baseline_days * 86400
  }
  if (sum(base) < 5) base <- ok
  if (sum(base) < 5) return(tibble())

  robust_sd <- function(x) pmax(mad(x), 0.1 * abs(median(x)), 1e-6)  # floor avoids tiny MAD
  f %>% mutate(
    z_noise = (noise - median(noise[base])) / robust_sd(noise[base]),
    z_level = (median(level[base]) - level)   / robust_sd(level[base]),   # positive = lower than usual
    flag    = ok & (z_noise > cfg$z_noise |
                    (z_level > cfg$z_level & z_noise > cfg$z_level_noise_min)),
    session_start = min(d$gluc_time),
    session_end   = max(d$gluc_time)
  )
}

# Merge flagged windows into segments for ONE subject-session
make_segments <- function(f, cfg) {
  fl <- f %>% filter(flag)
  if (nrow(fl) == 0) return(tibble())
  s <- as.numeric(fl$win_start); e <- as.numeric(fl$win_end)
  prev_max <- c(-Inf, head(cummax(e), -1))
  grp <- cumsum(s - prev_max > cfg$merge_gap_h * 3600)

  fl %>%
    mutate(grp = grp) %>%
    group_by(grp) %>%
    summarise(seg_start   = min(win_start),
              seg_end     = min(max(win_end), first(session_end)),
              n_windows   = n(),
              max_z_noise = max(z_noise),
              max_z_level = max(z_level),
              session_end = first(session_end),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(duration_h = as.numeric(difftime(seg_end, seg_start, units = "hours")),
           runs_to_sensor_end = seg_end >= session_end - cfg$window_h * 3600) %>%
    filter(duration_h >= cfg$min_seg_h) %>%
    select(-grp, -session_end)
}
```

## Run detection

```{r run}
scored <- dat %>%
  group_by(subject, session) %>%
  group_modify(~ score_session(.x, cfg)) %>%
  ungroup()

segments <- scored %>%
  group_by(subject, session) %>%
  group_modify(~ make_segments(.x, cfg)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Result: flagged segments

```{r result}
segments %>% mutate(across(c(duration_h, max_z_noise, max_z_level), ~ round(.x, 1)))
```

As a list, one element per subject (subjects with no flagged segment are included as empty):

```{r result-list}
all_subjects <- unique(dat$subject)
flagged_list <- map(setNames(all_subjects, all_subjects), function(s) {
  segments %>% filter(subject == s) %>% select(seg_start, seg_end, duration_h)
})
flagged_list
```

Subjects with at least one flagged segment:

```{r flagged-subjects}
unique(segments$subject)
```

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
write.csv(segments, "flagged_segments.csv", row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(flagged_list, "flagged_segments_list.rds")
```

## Visual check

Red shading = flagged segment.

```{r plots, fig.height=3.2}
walk(all_subjects, function(s) {
  p <- ggplot(filter(dat, subject == s), aes(gluc_time, gl)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.2) +
    geom_rect(data = filter(segments, subject == s),
              aes(xmin = seg_start, xmax = seg_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
    labs(title = paste("Subject", s), x = "Time", y = "Glucose") +
    theme_minimal()
  print(p)
})
```

Window-level diagnostics (useful for tuning thresholds):

```{r diag, fig.height=5}
scored %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(z_noise, z_level), names_to = "metric", values_to = "z") %>%
  ggplot(aes(win_start, z, colour = metric)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(cfg$z_noise), linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ subject, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Tuning notes

- **Too many false positives:** raise `z_noise` / `min_seg_h`, or lengthen `window_h`.
- **Missing subtle deterioration:** lower `z_noise` to about 2.5, or use `baseline_days = 5` so that a long deteriorated tail does not contaminate the baseline.
- The baseline is the session's median, so this works when less than about half of the session is deteriorated. If a sensor is bad for most of its life, use `baseline_days`.
- Segment start is accurate to about `window_h` (the first flagged window's start), because windows overlap. Reduce `window_h` and `step_h` for sharper onset estimates.
- `runs_to_sensor_end = TRUE` means the segment lasts until the last reading of the session, which is the typical end-of-life failure.
